subject.title: feat(chat-ui): syntax-highlighted code blocks and native tables in chat markdown

question: Should OpenClaw accept a swift-markdown and swift-cmark-backed shared Apple chat renderer for iOS and macOS after the license, changelog, and proof blockers are fixed?
rationale: The PR adds a new visible native rendering strategy and app dependency under an open product-decision-labeled mobile Markdown issue, so automation can identify the blockers but should not choose the permanent renderer direction.

options.title: Sponsor After Cleanup And Proof
options.body: Keep the PR open, require license notices, changelog cleanup, and inspectable native UI proof, then review the renderer direction for merge.

options.title: Narrow The Apple Renderer Scope
options.body: Ask for a smaller PR that fixes the urgent table/code readability gap while deferring broader native Markdown rendering behavior.

options.title: Pause The Native Renderer
options.body: Pause or close the branch if maintainers do not want this parser dependency or renderer strategy in the bundled Apple apps.

recommendation.title: Sponsor After Cleanup And Proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, require license notices, changelog cleanup, and inspectable native UI proof, then review the renderer direction for merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-main history match for the shared chat renderer path and is already carrying the linked product-direction work.
